data.gender_notes: Fey is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Fey was a goddess of the forest and nature. Her name derives from the Greek word for 'mist' or 'fog', symbolizing the mystery and enchantment of the natural world. In Christianity, Fey is sometimes associated with the Virgin Mary, representing the hidden wisdom and grace within. The name Fey carries the meaning “Mystery, Enchantment” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Fey usually hope their child will grow to embody mystery, enchantment and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of the divine mystery hidden within nature and ourselves.
data.etymology: Fey belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mystery, Enchantment.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fey total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.
